置信区间与区间统计量
Confidence Intervals and Interval Statistics

Page 1

1 Learning Goals

  1. Be able to determine whether an expression defines a valid interval statistic.
  2. Be able to compute z and t confidence intervals for the mean given normal data.
  3. Be able to compute the χ2 confidence interval for the variance given normal data.
  4. Be able to define the confidence level of a confidence interval.
  5. Be able to explain the relationship between the z confidence interval (and confidence level) and the z non-rejection region (and significance level) in NHST.

本讲把点估计扩展为区间估计. 三条计算公式分别处理: 已知 σ 时的均值、未知 σ 时的均值、未知 σ2 时的方差. 更重要的是理解置信水平和显著性检验的关系.

Page 1

2 Introduction

We continue to survey the tools of frequentist statistics. Suppose we have a model (probability distribution) for observed data with an unknown parameter. We have seen how NHST uses data to test the hypothesis that the unknown parameter has a particular value. We have also seen how point estimates like the MLE use data to provide an estimate of the unknown parameter. On its own, a point estimate like xˉ=2.2 carries no information about its accuracy; it’s just a single number, regardless of whether its based on ten data points or one million data points.

For this reason, statisticians augment point estimates with confidence intervals. For example, to estimate an unknown mean μ we might be able to say that our best estimate of the mean is xˉ=2.2 with a 95% confidence interval [1.2,3.2]. Another way to describe the interval is: xˉ±1.

We will leave to later the explanation of exactly what the 95% confidence level means. For now, we’ll note that taken together the width of the interval and the confidence level provide a measure on the strength of the evidence supporting the hypothesis that the μ is close to our estimate xˉ. You should think of the confidence level of an interval as analogous to the significance level of a NHST. As explained below, it is no accident that we often see significance level α=0.05 and confidence level 0.95=1−α.

We will first explore confidence intervals in situations where you will easily be able to compute by hand: z and t confidence intervals for the mean and χ2 confidence intervals for the variance. We will use R to handle all the computations in more complicated cases. Indeed, the challenge with confidence intervals is not their computation, but rather interpreting them correctly and knowing how to use them in practice.

置信区间 confidence interval 给出参数的区间估计. 点估计 xˉ=2.2 本身不显示精度; 区间宽度补充这方面的信息, 置信水平则描述这种方法在重复抽样中的表现.

频率派的置信水平和贝叶斯后验概率不是一回事. 对已经算出的固定区间, 不能说未知参数有 95% 的概率落在里面.

原文笔误: “regardless of whether its based on” 应为 “regardless of whether it’s based on”, 即 it is 的缩写.
Page 2

3 Interval statistics

Recall that our definition of a statistic is anything that can be computed from data. In particular, the formula for a statistic cannot include unknown quantities.

Example 1. Suppose x1​,…,xn​ is drawn from N(μ,σ2) where μ and σ are unknown.

  1. xˉ and xˉ−5 are statistics.
  2. xˉ−μ is not a statistic since μ is unknown.
  3. If μ0​ a known value, then xˉ−μ0​ is a statistic. This case arises when we consider the null hypothesis μ=μ0​. For example, if the null hypothesis is μ=5, then the statistic xˉ−μ0​ is just xˉ−5 from (i).

We can play the same game with intervals to define interval statistics

Example 2. Suppose x1​,…,xn​ is drawn from N(μ,σ2) where μ is unknown.

  1. The interval [xˉ−2.2,xˉ+2.2]=xˉ±2.2 is an interval statistic.
  2. If σ is known, then [xˉ−n​2σ​,xˉ+n​2σ​] is an interval statistic.
  3. On the other hand, if σ is unknown then [xˉ−n​2σ​,xˉ+n​2σ​] is not an interval statistic.
  4. If s2 is the sample variance, then [xˉ−n​2s​,xˉ+n​2s​] is an interval statistic because s2 is computed from the data.

We will return to (ii) and (iv), as these are respectively the z and t confidence intervals for estimating μ.

区间统计量 interval statistic 的上下端点都必须能由数据和已知量算出. 含未知 μ 或未知 σ 的表达式不行; 把未知 σ 换成样本标准差 s 后就可以.

所以 z 区间要求 σ 已知, t 区间用 s 代替它. 这不是记号偏好, 而是统计量定义的要求.

原文笔误: Example 1(iii) 的 “If μ0​ a known value” 缺谓语, 应为 “If μ0​ is a known value”.
Page 2

Technically an interval statistic is nothing more than a pair of point statistics giving the lower and upper bounds of the interval. Our reason for emphasizing that the interval is a statistic is to highlight the following:

  1. The interval is random – new random data will produce a new interval.
  2. As frequentists, we are perfectly happy using it because it doesn’t depend on the value of an unknown parameter or hypothesis.
  3. As usual with frequentist statistics we have to assume a certain hypothesis, e.g. value of μ, before we can compute probabilities about the interval.

Example 3. Suppose we draw n samples x1​,…,xn​ from a N(μ,1) distribution, where μ is unknown. Suppose we wish to know the probability that 0 is in the interval [xˉ−2,xˉ+2]. Without knowing the value of μ this is impossible. However, we can compute this probability for any given (hypothesized) value of μ.

  1. A warning which will be repeated: Be careful in your thinking about these probabilities. Confidence intervals are a frequentist notion. Since frequentists do not compute probabilities of hypotheses, the confidence level is never a probability that the unknown parameter is in the specific confidence interval computed from the given data.

随机的是区间, 不是固定参数. 新样本会改变 xˉ, 从而改变整个区间. 在指定 μ 后, 才能计算随机区间覆盖某个值的概率.

Example 3 中 0∈[xˉ−2,xˉ+2] 等价于 xˉ∈[−2,2]. 但 xˉ 的分布依赖未知的 μ, 所以只给区间而完全不设定 μ, 无法给出这个概率.

Review of critical values and quantiles

  • Quantile: left tail P(X<qα​)=α
  • Critical value: right tail P(X>cα​)=α

Letters for critical values:

  • zα​ for N(0,1)
  • tα​ for t distributions
  • cα​,xα​ all purpose

分位数 quantile 按左尾面积标记, 临界值 critical value 按右尾面积标记. 因而 qα​=z1−α​. 例如 q0.975​=z0.025​=1.96.

双尾区间把 α 平分到两侧, 所以公式用 zα/2​, 不是 zα​.

1. z0.025​=
(a) -1.96   (b) -0.95   (c) 0.95   (d) 1.96   (e) 2.87

(a) -1.33   (b) -0.99   (c) 0.99   (d) 1.33   (e) 3.52

z Confidence Intervals for the Mean

Page 3

4 z confidence intervals for the mean

Throughout this section we will assume that we have normally distributed data:

x1​,x2​,…,xn​∼N(μ,σ2).

As we often do, we will introduce the main ideas through examples, building on what we know about rejection and non-rejection regions in NHST until we have constructed a confidence interval.

4.1 Definition of z confidence intervals for the mean

We start with z confidence intervals for the mean. First we’ll give the formula. Then we’ll walk through the derivation in one entirely numerical example. This will give us the basic idea. Then we’ll repeat this example, replacing the explicit numbers by symbols. Finally we’ll work through a computational example.

Definition: Suppose the data x1​,…,xn​∼N(μ,σ2), with unknown mean μ and known variance σ2. The (1−α) confidence interval for μ is

[xˉ−n​zα/2​σ​,xˉ+n​zα/2​σ​],

where zα/2​ is the right critical value P(Z>zα/2​)=α/2.

For example, if α=0.05 then zα/2​=1.96 so the 0.95 (or 95%) confidence interval is

[xˉ−n​1.96σ​,xˉ+n​1.96σ​].

We’ve created an applet that generates normal data and displays the corresponding z confidence interval for the mean. It also shows the t-confidence interval, as discussed in the next section. Play around to get a sense for random intervals!
https://mathlets.org/mathlets/confidence-intervals/

区间中心是 xˉ, 半径是 zα/2​σ/n​. 其中 σ/n​ 是样本均值的标准误, 临界值决定覆盖标准误的倍数.

前提包括独立正态数据和已知 σ2. 置信水平 1−α 与双尾检验的显著性水平 α 互补.

Page 3

Example 4. Suppose we collect 100 data points from a N(μ,32) distribution and the sample mean is xˉ=12. Give the 95% confidence interval for μ.

Solution: Using formula 1, this is trivial to compute: the 95% confidence interval for μ is

[xˉ−n​1.96σ​,xˉ+n​1.96σ​]=[12−101.96⋅3​,12+101.96⋅3​].

代入时先用 N(μ,32) 辨认出 σ=3, 再用 n​=100​=10. 半径因此是 1.96⋅3/10, 区间中心保持 12 不变.

Pages 3–4

4.2 Explaining the definition part 1: non-rejection regions

Our next goal is to explain the definition 1 starting from our knowledge of rejection/non-rejection regions in NHST. The phrase ‘non-rejection region’ is not pretty, but we will discipline ourselves to use it instead of the inacurate phrase ‘acceptance region’.

Example 5. Suppose that n=12 data points are drawn from N(μ,52) where μ is unknown. As usual, call the average of the data xˉ. Set up a two-sided z-test of H0​:μ=2.71 at significance level α=0.05. Describe the rejection and non-rejection regions.

Solution: Under the null hypothesis (μ=2.71) we have

z=5/12​xˉ−2.71​∼N(0,1).

We know that, for α=0.05, the non-rejection region for z is [−1.96,1.96]. That is, we do not reject if, assuming H0​, z is within two standard deviations of the standardized mean. By definition, this means

P(−1.96≤z≤1.96∣μ=2.71)=0.95.

And, the rejection region is

(−∞,−1.96)∪(1.96,∞).

For confidence intervals, we will want to unwind the definition of z and write the regions in terms of xˉ. This allows us to directly use the natural statistic xˉ.

先在标准化尺度上写区域, 再换回 xˉ 的尺度. 非拒绝域是 ∣z∣≤1.96, 两侧尾部合起来对应 α=0.05.

这里用「不拒绝」而不是「接受」, 因为落在非拒绝域并不证明 H0​ 为真.

原文笔误: “inacurate” 应为 “inaccurate”.
Pages 4–5

Example 6. Redo the previous example using xˉ as the test statistic.

Solution: Under the null hypothesis (μ=2.71) we have xi​∼N(2.71,52) and thus

xˉ∼N(2.71,52/12)

where 52/12 is the variance xˉ. We know that for normal data, significance α=0.05 corresponds to a rejection region starting 1.96 standard deviations from the hypothesized mean. That is,

Non-rejection region: We do not reject H0​ if xˉ is in the interval

[2.71−12​1.96⋅5​,2.71+12​1.96⋅5​]=[−0.12,5.54].

That is, we do not reject if, assuming H0​, xˉ is within two standard deviations of the hypothesized mean. By definition, this means

P(−0.12≤xˉ≤5.54∣μ=2.71)=0.95.

Rejection region:

(−∞,2.71−12​1.96⋅5​]∪[2.71+12​1.96⋅5​,∞)=(−∞,−0.12]∪[5.54,∞).

The following figure shows the rejection and non-rejection regions for xˉ. The regions represent ranges of xˉ so they are represented by the colored bars on the xˉ axis. The area of the shaded region in the tails is the significance level.

读图: 曲线是 H0​ 下 xˉ 的分布, 不是原始单个观测的分布. 蓝条的半宽为 1.96⋅5/12​, 橙色尾部的总面积为 0.05.

幻灯片小错: Example 6 把拒绝域写成含端点的 (−∞,−0.12]∪[5.54,∞), 与 Example 5 的开区间及其闭的非拒绝域矛盾. 应为 (−∞,−0.12)∪(5.54,∞). 连续分布中端点概率为 0, 所以概率不变, 但集合定义不能重叠.
Page 5

Example 7. Suppose that n data points are drawn from N(μ,σ2) where μ is unknown and σ is known. Set up a two-sided significance test of H0​:μ=μ0​ using the statistic xˉ at significance level α. Describe the rejection and non-rejection regions.

Solution: Under the null hypothesis μ=μ0​ we have xi​∼N(μ0​,σ2) and thus

xˉ∼N(μ0​,σ2/n),

where σ2/n is the variance (σxˉ​)2 of xˉ and μ0​,σ and n are all known values.

Let zα/2​ be the critical value: P(Z>zα/2​)=α/2. Then the non-rejection and rejection regions are separated by the values of xˉ that are zα/2​⋅σxˉ​ from the hypothesized mean. Since σxˉ​=σ/n​ we have

Non-rejection region: we do not reject H0​ if xˉ is in the interval

[μ0​−n​zα/2​σ​,μ0​+n​zα/2​σ​].

Rejection region:

(−∞,μ0​−n​zα/2​σ​]∪[μ0​+n​zα/2​σ​,∞).

一般形式只是把 2.71、5 和 12 换成 μ0​,σ,n. 非拒绝域以假设值 μ0​ 为中心; 后面的置信区间则以观测值 xˉ 为中心, 两者半径相同.

幻灯片小错: Example 7 的拒绝域也把边界写进两侧区间, 同时又把同一边界写进非拒绝域. 与非拒绝域的闭区间配套时, 拒绝域应为两个开区间.

从非拒绝域到置信区间
From Non-rejection Regions to Confidence Intervals

Pages 5–6

4.3 Manipulating intervals: algebraic pivoting

We need to get comfortable manipulating intervals. In general, we will make use of the type of ‘obvious’ statements that can be hard to get across. First is the notion of pivoting. Stripping away the statistical terms, pivoting is the following algebraic maneuver.

Example 8. Algebraic pivoting. Suppose we have two variables a and b. Suppose also that a is in the interval [b−4,b+6]. Show that b is in the interval [a−6,a+4].

Solution: We are given, b−4≤a≤b+6. Therefore,

−4≤a−b≤6⇒4≥b−a≥−6⇒a+4≥b≥a−6.QED

This is called pivoting because the roles of a and b are reversed along with the direction of the inequalities.

In the example above, the ranges on either side of b are different. Quite often they will be the same. Here are some simple numerical examples of pivoting for symmetric intervals.

Example 9. (i) 1.5 is in the interval [0−2.3,0+2.3], so 0 is in the interval [1.5−2.3,1.5+2.3]
(ii) Likewise 1.5 is not in the interval [0−1,0+1], so 0 is not in the interval [1.5−1,1.5+1].

反转 pivoting 是交换「中心」和「被判断是否落入区间的点」. 对称区间中, a∈[b−r,b+r] 与 b∈[a−r,a+r] 都表示 ∣a−b∣≤r.

非对称区间也能反转, 但左右距离要交叉: 左边的 4 变成右边的 4, 右边的 6 变成左边的 6.

Pages 6–7

4.4 Pivoting non-rejection intervals to confidence intervals

For normal data, the non-rejection region for xˉ is an interval centered on μ0​. By pivoting, we get the confidence interval for μ centered on xˉ.

Example 10. Suppose we have n data points with a sample mean xˉ and hypothesized mean μ0​=2.71. Suppose also that the null distribution is xi​∼N(μ0​,32). Then with a significance level of 0.05 we have:

(1a) The non-rejection region is centered on μ0​=2.71. That is, we don’t reject H0​ if xˉ is in the interval

[μ0​−n​1.96σ​,μ0​+n​1.96σ​].

(1b) Assuming the null hypothesis we have

P(xˉ is in the non-rejection region∣H0​)=1−α=0.95.

That is,

P(μ0​−n​1.96σ​≤xˉ≤μ0​+n​1.96σ​∣H0​)=0.95.

(2a) Pivoting (1a) gives: we don’t reject H0​ if μ0​ is in the interval

[xˉ−n​1.96σ​,xˉ+n​1.96σ​].

(2b) Pivoting (1b) gives: assuming the null hypothesis we have

P(xˉ−n​1.96σ​≤μ0​≤xˉ+n​1.96σ​∣H0​)=0.95.

The interval in (2a) is called the 0.95 confidence interval for μ. It is centered on xˉ, it has the same width as the non-rejection region.

Again, notice the symmetry: the statement ‘xˉ is in the non-rejection interval around μ0​’ is equivalent to ‘μ0​ is in the confidence interval [xˉ−1.96σ,xˉ+1.96σ] around xˉ’.

Here is a visualization of pivoting from intervals around μ0​ to intervals around xˉ. In the figures, μ0​=1 and xˉ=1.5. The first pair of intervals have width 2 and the second pair have width 4.6.

The first pair of intervals shows the interval μ0​±1 pivoted to the interval xˉ±1. Since xˉ is not in the first interval, μ0​ is not in the pivoted interval. In the second pair of intervals, since xˉ is in the interval μ0​±2.3, we see μ0​ is in the pivoted interval xˉ±2.3.

两个写法是同一个不等式, 所以覆盖概率没有因反转而改变. 变化的是解释角度: 检验问 xˉ 是否落在 μ0​ 周围, 区间估计问 μ0​ 是否落在 xˉ 周围.

图中的两对区间半径分别相同. 一个包含对方中心, 另一个也必然包含; 一个不包含, 另一个也必然不包含.

幻灯片小错: Example 10 最后的对称性句子把置信区间印成 [xˉ−1.96σ,xˉ+1.96σ], 漏掉了除以 n​. 应为 [xˉ−1.96σ/n​,xˉ+1.96σ/n​], 与同例前面的公式一致.
Pages 7–8

4.5 Summary of normal confidence intervals: definition and properties

Suppose x1​,x2​,…,xn​ are independent data from a N(μ,σ2) distribution. We assume μ is unknown, but σ is known.

  • Definition. The 1−α confidence interval for μ is
    [xˉ−n​zα/2​σ​,xˉ+n​zα/2​σ​],
    where zα/2​ is standard normal α/2 critical value.
  • The confidence interval only depends on xˉ and known values, so it is a statistic.
  • The confidence interval is random: different data generate different intervals.
  • If the null hypothesis is μ=μ0​, then the confidence interval is found by pivoting the non-rejection region. If μ0​ is in the 1−α confidence interval, then we do not reject H0​ at significance level α. Likewise, we do reject H0​ at significance level α if μ0​ is not in the 1−α confidence interval.
  • Assuming H0​, then in 95% of random trials the 95% confidence interval will contain μ0​.

The following figure illustrates how we don’t reject H0​ if the confidence interval around xˉ contains μ0​ and we reject H0​ if the confidence interval doesn’t contain μ0​. There is a lot in the figure so we will list carefully what you are seeing:

  1. We started with the figure from Example 6 which shows the null distribution for μ0​=2.71 and the rejection and non-rejection regions.
  2. We added two possible values of the statistic xˉ, i.e. xˉ1​ and xˉ2​, and their confidence intervals. Note that the width of each interval is exactly the same as the width of the non-rejection region since both use ±1.96⋅5/12​.

The first value, xˉ1​, is in the non-rejection region and its interval includes the null hypothesis μ0​=2.71. This illustrates that not rejecting H0​ corresponds to the confidence interval containing μ0​.

The second value, xˉ2​, is in the rejection region and its interval does not contain μ0​. This illustrates that rejecting H0​ corresponds to the confidence interval not containing μ0​.

We can still wring one more essential observation out of this example. Our choice of null hypothesis μ=2.71 was completely arbitrary. If we replace μ=2.71 by any other hypothesis μ=μ0​ then the confidence interval is the same, i.e. it does not depend on any hypothesis.

95% 的含义是重复抽样的覆盖率: 若同一真值 μ0​ 下反复抽样并按同一规则建区间, 长期约 95% 的区间会覆盖 μ0​. 不是某一个已算出的区间有 95% 的后验概率.

置信区间本身不含 μ0​, 所以不依赖选定哪个零假设. 但它可以反过来给出所有「不会在水平 α 下被拒绝」的 μ0​.

Pages 8–9

4.6 Explaining the definition part 3: translating a general non-rejection region to a confidence interval

Note that the specific values of σ and n in the preceding example were of no particular consequence, so they can be replaced by their symbols. In this way we can take Example 7 quickly through the same steps as Example 6.

In words, Equation 2 and the corresponding figure say that we don’t reject if xˉ is in the interval μ0​±zα/2​σ/n​. This is exactly equivalent to saying that we don’t reject if μ0​ is in the interval xˉ±zα/2​σ/n​.

We can rewrite equation 3 as: at significance level α we don’t reject if the interval

[xˉ−n​zα/2​σ​,xˉ+n​zα/2​σ​]

contains μ0​.

We call the interval 4 a (1−α) confidence interval because, assuming μ=μ0​, on average it will contain μ0​ in the fraction (1−α) of random trials.

The following figure illustrates the point that μ0​ is in the (1−α) confidence interval around xˉ is equivalent to xˉ is in the non-rejection region (at significance level α) for H0​:μ0​=μ. The figure shows xˉ1​ is in the non-rejection region for μ0​, so the confidence interval around xˉ1​ contains μ0​. Similarly, xˉ2​ is not in the non-rejection region for μ0​, so the confidence interval around xˉ2​ does not contain μ0​.

Note, that the confidence intervals and the non-rejection region all have the same width!

这一节把数值例子推广成一般等价关系:

μ0​∈[xˉ−zα/2​n​σ​,xˉ+zα/2​n​σ​]⟺xˉ∈[μ0​−zα/2​n​σ​,μ0​+zα/2​n​σ​].

左边是置信区间判据, 右边是双尾检验的非拒绝判据.

Slide 8

Conceptual view of confidence intervals

  • Computed from data ⇒ interval statistic
  • ‘Estimates’ a parameter of interest ⇒ interval estimate
  • Width = measure of precision
  • Confidence level = measure of performance
  • Connected to NHST: Given a test statistic xˉ, the confidence interval for θ = all values θ0​ for which we wouldn’t reject the null hypothesis θ=θ0​.
  • Confidence intervals are a frequentist method.
    • No need for a prior, only uses likelihood.
    • Frequentists do not assign probabilities to hypothetical values of unknown parameters.
    • A 95% confidence interval of [1.1,3.3] for μ does not mean that P(1.1≤μ≤3.3)=0.95.
  • We will compare with Bayesian probability intervals later.

Applet: https://mathlets.org/mathlets/confidence-intervals/

宽度描述精度, 置信水平描述方法表现, 两者不能混成「这个区间的概率」. 与贝叶斯区间相比, 频率派方法不需要先验, 也不给参数假设分配概率.

Slide 9

Discussion: Width of confidence intervals

The quantities n,c=confidence,xˉ,σ all appear in the z confidence interval for the mean.

How does the width of a confidence interval for the mean change if:

  1. We increase n and leave the others unchanged?
  2. We increase c and leave the others unchanged?
  3. We increase μ and leave the others unchanged?
  4. We increase σ and leave the others unchanged?

(A) it gets wider   (B) it gets narrower   (C) it stays the same.

答案依次为 B, A, C, A. 全宽为 2zα/2​σ/n​. n 增大使宽度按 1/n​ 缩小; 置信水平提高使临界值增大; σ 增大使区间变宽. μ 只影响位置, 不出现在宽度公式里.

z、t 与卡方区间的计算
Computing z, t and Chi-square Intervals

Slide 6

z rule of thumb

Suppose x1​,…,xn​∼N(μ,σ2) with σ known.

The rule-of-thumb 95% confidence interval for μ is:

[xˉ−2n​σ​,xˉ+2n​σ​].

A more precise 95% confidence interval for μ is:

[xˉ−1.96n​σ​,xˉ+1.96n​σ​].

2 是 1.96 的便于心算的近似. 粗略区间稍宽, 精确计算或正式报告时应使用相应临界值, 不把经验法则当成定义.

Pages 9–10

4.7 Computational example

Example 11. Suppose the data 2.5, 5.5, 8.5, 11.5 was drawn from a N(μ,102) distribution with unknown mean μ.

(a) Compute the point estimate xˉ for μ and the corresponding 50%, 80% and 95% confidence intervals.

(b) Consider the null hypothesis μ=1. Would you reject H0​ at α=0.05? α=0.20? α=0.50? Do these two ways: first by checking if the hypothesized value of μ is in the relevant confidence interval and second by constructing a rejection region.

Solution: (a) We compute that xˉ=7.0. The critical points are z0.025​=qnorm(0.975)=1.96, z0.1​=qnorm(0.9)=1.28, z0.25​=qnorm(0.75)=0.67. Since n=4 we have xˉ∼N(μ,102/4), i.e. σxˉ​=5. So we have:

  • 95% conf. interval =[xˉ−z0.025​σxˉ​,xˉ+z0.025​σxˉ​]=[7−1.96⋅5,7+1.96⋅5]=[−2.8,16.8]
  • 80% conf. interval =[xˉ−z0.1​σxˉ​,xˉ+z0.1​σxˉ​]=[7−1.28⋅5,7+1.28⋅5]=[0.6,13.4]
  • 50% conf. interval =[xˉ−z0.75​σxˉ​,xˉ+z0.75​σxˉ​]=[7−0.67⋅5,7+0.67⋅5]=[3.65,10.35]

Each of these intervals is a range estimate of μ. Notice that the higher the confidence level, the wider the interval needs to be.

(b) Since μ=1 is in the 95% and 80% confidence intervals, we would not reject the null hypothesis at the α=0.05 or α=0.20 levels. Since μ=1 is not in the 50% confidence interval, we would reject H0​ at the α=0.5 level.

We construct the rejection regions using the same critical values as in part (a). The difference is that rejection regions are intervals centered on the hypothesized value for μ: μ0​=1 and confidence intervals are centered on xˉ. Here are the rejection regions.

  • α=0.05⇒(−∞,μ0​−z0.025​σxˉ​]∪[μ0​+z0.025​σxˉ​,∞)=(−∞,−8.8]∪[10.8,∞)
  • α=0.20⇒(−∞,μ0​−z0.1​σxˉ​]∪[μ0​+z0.1​σxˉ​,∞)=(−∞,−5.4]∪[7.4,∞)
  • α=0.25⇒(−∞,μ0​−z0.25​σxˉ​]∪[μ0​+z0.25​σxˉ​,∞)=(−∞,−2.35]∪[4.35,∞)

To to do the NHST we must check whether or not xˉ=7 is in the rejection region.

  • α=0.05: 7<10.8 is not in the rejection region. We do not reject the hypothesis that μ=1 at a significance level of 0.05.
  • α=0.2: 7<7.4 is not in the rejection region. We do not reject the hypothesis that μ=1 at a significance level of 0.2.
  • α=0.5: 7>4.35 is in the rejection region. We reject the hypothesis that μ=1 at a significance level 0.5.

We get the same answers using either method.

同一组临界值可用于两种判断. 置信区间以 xˉ=7 为中心, 拒绝域以 μ0​=1 为中心. 置信水平越高, 区间越宽; 相应地, 显著性水平越小, 拒绝域越靠外.

原文用两位临界值得到 50% 区间 [3.65,10.35]. 用更精确的 z0.25​=0.67449 会得到约 [3.63,10.37], 差别来自舍入.

幻灯片小错: Example 11(a) 的 50% 区间把 z0.25​ 误写成 z0.75​, 但同一行仍代入 z0.25​ 的数值 0.67. 正确公式使用 z0.25​.
幻灯片小错: Example 11(b) 第三个拒绝域标成 α=0.25, 应为题目和后续判断所用的 α=0.50. 双尾各侧为 0.25, 所以临界值仍是 z0.25​.
原文笔误: “To to do the NHST” 多了一个 “to”, 应为 “To do the NHST”.
Page 10

5 t-confidence intervals for the mean

This will be nearly identical to normal confidence intervals. In this setting σ is not known, so we have to make the following replacements.

  1. Use sxˉ​=s/n​ instead of σxˉ​=σ/n​. Here s is the sample variance we used before in t-tests
  2. Use t-critical values instead of z-critical values.

5.1 Definition of t-confidence intervals for the mean

Definition: Suppose that x1​,…,xn​∼N(μ,σ2), where the values of the mean μ and the standard deviation σ are both unknown. . The (1−α) confidence interval for μ is

[xˉ−n​tα/2​s​,xˉ+n​tα/2​s​],

here tα/2​ is the right critical value P(T>tα/2​)=α/2 for T∼t(n−1) and s2 is the sample variance of the data.

t 区间与 z 区间的结构相同, 但用 s 估计未知的 σ, 并使用自由度 n−1 的 Student t 分布. 估计标准差增加了不确定性, 所以相同样本量与置信水平下, t 临界值通常大于 z 临界值.

幻灯片小错: “Here s is the sample variance” 应为 “Here s is the sample standard deviation”. 样本方差是 s2, 同页定义后半句写对了.
原文笔误: “are both unknown. . The” 连续出现两个句点, 应只保留一个.
Pages 10–11

5.2 Construction of t confidence intervals

For t confidence intervals we repeat the construction of normal confidence intervals with σ replaced by its estimate s.

Suppose that n data points are drawn from N(μ,σ2) where μ and σ are unknown. We’ll derive the t confidence interval following the same pattern as for the z confidence interval. Under the null hypothesis μ=μ0​, we have xi​∼N(μ0​,σ2). So the studentized mean follows a Student t distribution with n−1 degrees of freedom:

t=s/n​xˉ−μ0​​∼t(n−1).

Let tα/2​ be the critical value: P(T>tα/2​)=α/2, where T∼t(n−1). We know from running one-sample t-tests that the non-rejection region is given by ∣t∣≤tα/2​.

Using the definition of the t-statistic to write the rejection region in terms of xˉ we get: at significance level α we don’t reject if

s/n​∣xˉ−μ0​∣​≤tα/2​⟺∣xˉ−μ0​∣≤tα/2​n​s​.

Geometrically, the right hand side says that we don’t reject if μ0​ is within tα/2​s/n​ of xˉ. This is exactly equivalent to saying that we don’t reject if the interval

[xˉ−n​tα/2​s​,xˉ+n​tα/2​s​]

contains μ0​.

This interval is the confidence interval defined in 5.

推导仍是不等式反转: ∣xˉ−μ0​∣≤tα/2​s/n​ 同时描述「xˉ 离 μ0​ 不远」和「μ0​ 落在 xˉ 的 t 区间内」.

Page 11

Example 12. Suppose the data 2.5, 5.5, 8.5, 11.5 was drawn from a N(μ,σ2) distribution with μ and σ both unknown.

Give interval estimates for μ by finding the 95%, 80% and 50% confidence intervals.

Solution: By direct computation we have xˉ=7 and s2=15. The critical points are t0.025​=qt(0.975)=3.18, t0.1​=qt(0.9)=1.64, and t0.25​=qt(0.75)=0.76.

  • 95% conf. interval =[xˉ−t0.025​s/n​,xˉ+t0.025​s/n​]=[0.84,13.16]
  • 80% conf. interval =[xˉ−t0.1​s/n​,xˉ+t0.1​s/n​]=[3.82,10.18]
  • 50% conf. interval =[xˉ−t0.25​s/n​,xˉ+t0.25​s/n​]=[5.53,8.47]

All of these confidence intervals give interval estimates for the value of μ. Again, notice that the higher the confidence level, the wider the corresponding interval.

与 Example 11 的数据相同, 但现在 σ 未知, 所以用 s2=15 和自由度 4−1=3 的 t 临界值. 这里不能再把 σ=10 当作已知量.

Pages 11–12

6 Chi-square confidence intervals for the variance

We now turn to an interval estimate for the unknown variance.

Definition: Suppose the data x1​,…,xn​ is drawn from N(μ,σ2) with mean μ and standard deviation σ both unknown. The (1−α) confidence interval for the variance σ2 is

[cα/2​(n−1)s2​,c1−α/2​(n−1)s2​].

Here cα/2​ is the right critical value P(X2>cα/2​)=α/2 for X2∼χ2(n−1) and s2 is the sample variance of the data.

The derivation of this interval is nearly identical to that of the previous derivations, now starting from the chi-square test for variance. The basic fact we need is that, for data drawn from N(μ,σ2), the statistic (n−1)s2/σ2 follows a chi-square distribution with n−1 degrees of freedom. So given the null hypothesis H0​:σ=σ0​, the test statistic is (n−1)s2/σ02​ and the non-rejection region at significance level α is

c1−α/2​<σ02​(n−1)s2​<cα/2​.

Pivoting algebra converts this to

c1−α/2​(n−1)s2​>σ02​>cα/2​(n−1)s2​.

This says we don’t reject if the interval

[cα/2​(n−1)s2​,c1−α/2​(n−1)s2​]

contains σ02​.

This is our (1−α) confidence interval.

A difference from the z and t confidence intervals is that this chi-square confidence intervals are not exactly symmetric around the estimator s2. The reason is that the chi-square distribution (with n−1 degrees of freedom) is not symmetric around its mean n−1.

因为 cα/2​>c1−α/2​, 用较大的 cα/2​ 作分母得到下界, 用较小的 c1−α/2​ 作分母得到上界. 取倒数时不等号方向随之反转.

这个区间估计的是 σ2, 一般不关于 s2 对称. 若要标准差 σ 的区间, 对两个正端点分别开平方即可.

原文笔误: “this chi-square confidence intervals are” 主谓不一致, 应为 “this chi-square confidence interval is”.

The data 4, 1, 2, 3 is drawn from N(μ,σ2) with μ unknown.

(a) Find a 90% z confidence interval for μ, given that σ=2.

For the remaining parts, suppose σ is unknown.

(b) Find a 90% t confidence interval for μ.

(c) Find a 90% χ2 confidence interval for σ2.

(d) Find a 90% χ2 confidence interval for σ.

(e) Given a normal sample with n=100,xˉ=12, and s=5, find the rule-of-thumb 95% confidence interval for μ.

共同准备: 前四个数据给出 n=4,xˉ=2.5,s2=5/3,s=1.290994. 90% 区间有 α=0.10, 所以两尾各为 0.05. Python 算出 z0.05​=1.644854, t0.05​(3)=2.353363, c0.05​(3)=7.814728, c0.95​(3)=0.351846.

(c) 方差: (n−1)s2=5, 所以区间为 [5/7.814728,5/0.351846]≈[0.640,14.211].

Board question: confidence intervals and non-rejection regions

Suppose x1​,…,xn​∼N(μ,σ2) with σ known.

Consider two intervals:

  1. The z confidence interval around xˉ at confidence level 1−α.
  2. The z non-rejection region for H0​:μ=μ0​ at significance level α.

Compute and sketch these intervals to show that: μ0​ is in the first interval ⟺xˉ is in the second interval.

Solution

Confidence interval: xˉ±zα/2​σ/n​.

Non-rejection region: μ0​±zα/2​σ/n​.

Since the intervals are the same width they either both contain the other’s center or neither one does.

令 r=zα/2​σ/n​. 两个命题分别等价于 ∣xˉ−μ0​∣≤r, 因而互相等价. 草图只需画两条等长区间: 一条以 xˉ 为中心, 一条以 μ0​ 为中心.

民意调查中的比例区间
Confidence Intervals for Polling

Slide 13

Polling: a binomial proportion confidence interval

Data x1​,…,xn​ from a Bernoulli(θ) distribution with θ unknown.

A conservative normal† (1−α) confidence interval for θ is given by

[xˉ−2n​zα/2​​,xˉ+2n​zα/2​​].

Proof uses the CLT and the observation σ=θ(1−θ)​≤1/2.

Political polls often give a margin-of-error of ±1/n​. This rule-of-thumb corresponds to a 95% confidence interval:

[xˉ−n​1​,xˉ+n​1​].

(The proof is in the class 23 notes.)

Conversely, a margin of error of ±0.05 means 400 people were polled.

† There are many types of binomial proportion confidence intervals.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_proportion_confidence_interval

这里 xˉ 是成功比例 θ^. 正态近似给出均值区间的一般形式, 再用 θ(1−θ)≤1/4 把未知标准差保守地换成最大值 1/2.

95% 经验法则把 z0.025​≈1.96 近似为 2, 半径便成为 1/n​. 媒体报道的误差范围通常指这个近似值, 不是参数真实偏差的保证.

Board question: Polling

For a poll to find the proportion θ of people supporting X we know that a (1−α) confidence interval for θ is given by

[xˉ−2n​zα/2​​,xˉ+2n​zα/2​​].

(a) How many people would you have to poll to have a margin of error of 0.01 with 95% confidence? (You can do this in your head.)

(b) How many people would you have to poll to have a margin of error of 0.01 with 80% confidence. (You’ll want R or other calculator here.)

(c) If n=900, compute the 95% and 80% confidence intervals for θ.

(a) 使用 95% 经验法则, 令 1/n​=0.01, 得 n=10000.

(b) 80% 区间用 z0.1​=1.281552. 由 z0.1​/(2n​)≤0.01, 得 n≥4105.936, 所以至少调查 4106 人.

(c) 题目没有给支持人数或 xˉ, 所以只能写成含样本比例的区间. 95% 经验法则给出 [xˉ−1/30,xˉ+1/30]≈[xˉ−0.03333,xˉ+0.03333]; 80% 区间给出 [xˉ−0.02136,xˉ+0.02136].
